source_text: Multa adversum gentem Dei molitur rex qui non novit Ioseph. Obsetricibus Hebraeorum praecipit: si masculus, occidite; si femina, vivificate. Timuerunt Deum et vivificabant masculos. Litterae amici putant historiam stare; nos legem spiritalem intelligimus. In feminis caro designatur, in viro sensus rationabilis. Pharao odit coelestia quaerentem; carnalia vivere cupit. Qui deliciis fluitant — masculos necat et feminas vivificat. Qui unus ex mille ad Deum convertitur, Pharao persequitur.
pass_a_gloss: Many against people of-God plots king who not knew Joseph. To-midwives of-Hebrews he-commands: if male, kill; if female, keep-alive. They-feared God and were-keeping-alive males. Friends of-letter think history to-stand; we spiritual law understand. In females flesh is-designated, in man rational sense. Pharaoh hates one seeking heavenly-things; carnal-things to-live he-desires. Who in-delights float — males he-kills and females keeps-alive. Who one from thousand to God is-converted, Pharaoh pursues.
pass_b_english: The king [[who did not know Joseph >> Bible:Exodus 1:8]] keeps inventing new arts against God’s people. He even turns midwives — whose craft is to save life — into instruments of death: [[kill the male; keep the female alive >> Bible:Exodus 1:15-16]]. They [[feared God and kept the males alive >> Bible:Exodus 1:17]]. Friends of the letter stumble here; we learn that the law is spiritual. Woman figures flesh and its affections; man the rational sense that can [[seek the things above >> Bible:Colossians 3:1]]. Pharaoh, [[prince of this world >> Bible:John 16:11]], hates that male mind and nourishes only what is carnal. When you see people given to luxury, know he is killing males and sparing females; when you see [[one of a thousand >> Bible:Ecclesiastes 7:28]] turn toward God, know Pharaoh pursues him with a thousand devices.
